reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: p0149 imposes a one-way blanket bar on Licensee assignment with no Affiliate/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Article XX(a) makes any Licensee Change of Control an automatic termination absent Licensor consent (with deemed-reasonable refusal) — both expressly listed walk-away positions in ASSIGN.

Redline reaches the playbook position: it adds the Affiliate/successor carve-out for Licensee, applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other consents, bars Licensor assignment to a Licensee competitor, states a Change of Control is not an assignment, and strips Licensor's change-of-control termination/consent/re-pricing right, replacing it with a notice obligation.

The rewrite preserves the operative surrounding text needed downstream — the 'CHANGE OF CONTROL' definition lead-in in Article XX and the successors-and-permitted-assigns sentence in p0149 — so no cross-references are orphaned.

Failed minimal-edit heuristics are acceptable here: both clauses are structurally one-sided (blanket prohibition; automatic termination trigger), so the rule cannot be satisfied without substantially recasting them; no gratuitous changes beyond the assignment/change-of-control bargain were made.

Making the carve-out mutual (Licensor may also assign to an Affiliate/successor, subject to the competitor bar) is a modest, symmetrical concession consistent with the fallback and does not fall below the walk-away line; only nit is the absence of an express written-notice requirement for permitted assignments.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position, explains both edits in two sentences, offers the fallback, and follows the required prefix and tone.
